goal: Test the specific bridge MEASURED_RST_OR_FILTER <-> SPECIFIC_PROTEI_DEVICE_OR_CONTROL_CHANNEL without conflating SORM surveillance, DPI policy enforcement, vendor proximity, or Russian remote control.

verdict.most_important_new_fact: PROTEI has a separate DPI platform with explicit blocking, URL blacklist/whitelist, scheduling, redirection, bandwidth/policy control and DNS whitelist enforcement capabilities; ETECSA is a documented PROTEI customer and PROTEI states its technologies/equipment have operated in Cuba since 2015.
verdict.most_important_negative_fact: PROTEI SORM-2 traffic-tap documentation describes monitoring-mode/passive interception that does not affect client traffic; therefore measured TCP RST censorship should not be attributed to SORM simply because SORM is present.

evidence_chain.detail: OONI tested ETECSA AS27725 in May-June 2017 and reported DPI technology serving blank block pages and injecting TCP resets to blocked sites; the blocking system was suspected to be located in Havana.
PROTEI states that Russian technologies and equipment operate successfully in Cuba and that Latin American installations began in 2015. PROTEI also identifies ETECSA as a customer.

Recorded Future assesses Cuba very likely procured SORM hardware/software from Russian providers, most notably PROTEI, citing INSS and company/customer evidence. INSS reports PROTEI/SORM-3 technology as associated with heightened Cuban repression, but does not technically bind a specific filtering event to a PROTEI appliance.

Official PROTEI DPI documentation states the platform can detect application-layer traffic, apply per-flow policies, block/categorize URLs, use URL blacklists/whitelists, schedule black/white-list actions, block sites by domain name, enforce DNS-server IP whitelists, redirect traffic, dynamically manage bandwidth and integrate with PCRF/external systems.

Official PROTEI SORM-2 traffic-tap and LIS documentation describes monitoring/passive interception and explicitly says insertion does not affect customer traffic/network switching. This weakens any direct inference SORM itself generated RST censorship.
No public source found in this pass names PROTEI_DPI as a product purchased or deployed by ETECSA, despite PROTEI's customer relationship and confirmed Cuban deployments.

No device fingerprint, reset TTL/IPID signature, block-page marker, management IP, rack/device photograph, procurement record, configuration export or vendor-specific protocol artifact currently ties the 2017 or 2021 Cuban censorship fingerprint to PROTEI_DPI.
No public evidence found connecting any Cuban filtering device to a Russian remote management endpoint or operational command channel.

temporal_bridge.protei_cuba_presence: since at least 2015 according to PROTEI's own 2022 Cuba/Latin-America statement

product_separation.PROTEI_SORM: surveillance/interception/storage/control-panel ecosystem; documented traffic tap/passive interception components do not by themselves explain active RST injection
product_separation.PROTEI_DPI: active packet-policy platform capable of selective blocking, allow/deny lists, traffic redirection, scheduling and bandwidth control; technically capable of implementing censorship-like policy
product_separation.rule: PROTEI_SORM presence cannot be substituted for evidence of PROTEI_DPI deployment.

next_killer_evidence: ETECSA or Cuban procurement/import/customs record naming PROTEI_DPI, PCRF/PCEF or related traffic-management product.
PROTEI case study, installation note, support ticket, CV, tender, maintenance record or technical presentation naming ETECSA and DPI.
Archived FIHAV/Informática exhibitor material specifying which PROTEI products were demonstrated or delivered to ETECSA.

Network fingerprint unique enough to compare with a known PROTEI_DPI deployment elsewhere, including RST packet characteristics, HTTP block-page behavior, TTL/IPID, TCP sequence behavior, TLS/SNI handling or DNS policy behavior.
Management/control endpoint, firmware artifact, device certificate, vendor banner or configuration export from Cuban network infrastructure.
Historical before/after deployment timing showing a censorship-mechanism change coincident with a documented PROTEI DPI installation.
anti_overclaim_rules: ETECSA customer of PROTEI != ETECSA customer of PROTEI_DPI.
Cuba likely has PROTEI SORM != PROTEI caused censorship resets.
PROTEI_DPI can block traffic != PROTEI_DPI is deployed in Cuba.
final_rule: The hunt produced a real capability-and-timeline bridge from PROTEI to Cuba, but not the required device-level causal bridge. The correct next target is evidence of PROTEI_DPI deployment or a vendor-specific packet/control fingerprint, not further general SORM evidence.
